object_types.name: Vendor
object_types.definition: A supplier from whom the business procures goods, services, or materials. Identified by a vendor number assigned at creation.

source_references.excerpt: The vendor record. It's the thing in the supplier master... Every vendor has a vendor number, it's generated when the record is created.

object_types.name: VendorNumber
object_types.definition: The unique identifier assigned to a vendor at record creation.

source_references.excerpt: Every vendor has a vendor number, it's generated when the record is created... It's the thing we quote in every conversation with AP.

object_types.name: VendorStatus
object_types.definition: The operational state of a vendor record.

source_references.excerpt: Draft, active, suspended... Every vendor is in exactly one of them.

object_types.name: LegalName
object_types.definition: The official legal name of a vendor.

source_references.excerpt: Legal name.

object_types.name: TaxID
object_types.definition: The tax identification number of a vendor. Not unique; multiple vendors may share the same tax ID.

source_references.excerpt: Tax ID... We have vendors with the same tax ID -- different legal entities under one parent that file together, or we've onboarded the same company twice by accident and nobody's merged them.

object_types.name: VendorAddress
object_types.definition: A physical address associated with a vendor. May be remit-to, ship-from, or legal address.

source_references.excerpt: Address, though we have three addresses really -- remit-to, ship-from, and the legal one, which are frequently different and frequently wrong.

object_types.name: SpendTier
object_types.definition: The procurement spend classification of a vendor based on spending volume.

source_references.excerpt: Every vendor has a tier. Bronze, silver, gold... Gold vendors are the ones we spend real money with, they get quarterly business reviews, better payment terms, a named relationship manager.

object_types.name: RiskTier
object_types.definition: The risk classification of a vendor based on compliance review, data exposure, geography, and supplier criticality.

source_references.excerpt: I use low, medium, high... I'm talking about risk. Low, medium, high, based on the review -- what data they touch, what geography they operate in, whether they're a sole source.

object_types.name: RiskReview
object_types.definition: A compliance assessment of a vendor covering risk factors, data exposure, geography, and strategic importance. Identified by review ID.

source_references.excerpt: Every active vendor has exactly one completed risk review... The review is its own record. It has a review ID, because we need to know who signed it and when, and auditors ask.

object_types.name: ReviewID
object_types.definition: The unique identifier for a risk review record.

source_references.excerpt: It has a review ID, because we need to know who signed it and when, and auditors ask.

object_types.name: Region
object_types.definition: A geographic region served by vendors or requiring regional contact management.

source_references.excerpt: one primary contact per region... Region code. EMEA, APAC, NA, LATAM.

object_types.name: RegionCode
object_types.definition: The code identifying a region.

source_references.excerpt: Region code. EMEA, APAC, NA, LATAM... Four regions, fixed?

object_types.name: Contact
object_types.definition: A person serving as the primary point of contact for a vendor in a specific region.

source_references.excerpt: Each vendor has one primary contact... it's one primary contact per region... You cannot have two people both flagged primary for the same vendor in the same region.

object_types.name: ContactID
object_types.definition: The unique identifier for a contact record.

source_references.excerpt: Each vendor has one primary contact. Name, email, phone number.

object_types.definition: The name of a contact person.

ambiguities.description: Active vendor requirement for risk review: The transcript states 'Every active vendor has exactly one completed risk review' but later clarifies 'a vendor accumulates review records over time. At most one is the current one. Being active requires a current signed-off review.' It is unclear whether a vendor becomes active once a review is completed, or whether there is a separate explicit action to move a vendor to active status. Does completing a review automatically move a vendor from draft to active, or is there a distinct approval step?

source_references.excerpt: Every active vendor has exactly one completed risk review... A vendor accumulates review records over time. At most one is the current one. Being active requires a current signed-off review.

ambiguities.description: Risk review signing-off process: The transcript mentions reviews are 'signed off' and require audit committee approval in at least one case, but does not define the process, who signs off, or the state model. Is a review 'completed and signed-off' a single combined state, or are there separate 'completed' and 'signed-off' phases? If separate, what blocks a PO from being raised before sign-off?

source_references.excerpt: A vendor cannot be moved to active until a risk review has been completed and signed off... Every active vendor has exactly one completed risk review.

ambiguities.description: Vendor address granularity: The transcript mentions vendors have three types of addresses (remit-to, ship-from, legal) that are 'frequently different and frequently wrong.' It is unclear whether these are three separate address slots on the vendor record, or a single address field with an address type selector. Should these be modeled as three separate attributes, or as a single address with a type discriminator?

source_references.excerpt: Address, though we have three addresses really -- remit-to, ship-from, and the legal one, which are frequently different and frequently wrong.

ambiguities.description: Tax documentation requirements: The transcript refers to 'tax documentation' and specifically mentions 'W-9' but does not establish whether other forms (e.g., foreign tax documentation) may be required, or whether a single W-9 is always sufficient. Are multiple tax forms required, or is W-9 the universal form? The discussion shifts from 'W-9 on file' to 'risk review completion' as the gate to active status, but tax documentation and risk review are not explicitly linked.

source_references.excerpt: Once the W-9 is in, they're live... A vendor cannot be moved to active until a risk review has been completed and signed off.

ambiguities.description: Contact mandatory participation in vendor-region: The model captures 'Vendor operates in Region with Contact' and marks Contact as mandatory, meaning every such fact must have a contact. However, the transcript states 'If they don't operate in that region, there's nothing there at all.' This implies a vendor may not operate in certain regions. Should Contact be optional (a vendor may operate in a region with no primary contact assigned), or mandatory (a vendor operating in a region must have an assigned contact)?

source_references.excerpt: Can a vendor have no contact in a region?... If they don't operate in that region, there's nothing there at all.

ambiguities.description: Identification by tax ID versus vendor number: The transcript establishes vendor number as the identifier, but stakeholders also note vendors can accidentally be onboarded twice (duplicates with the same tax ID and legal entity). There is tension between tax ID being logically unique (one tax ID per legal entity) and practically non-unique (duplicates exist). Should tax ID be modeled as a candidate key (alternative identifier) or remain unambiguously non-unique? The cleanup project is out of scope, but the data quality issue affects constraint design.

source_references.excerpt: Could you identify a vendor by tax ID instead?... We have vendors with the same tax ID... Tax ID isn't an identifier, vendor number is.

ambiguities.description: Spend tier assignment process: The transcript states 'Every vendor gets a spend tier. Bronze by default if nobody's assessed them.' This implies bronze is a default for newly created vendors, but it is unclear whether bronze is assigned automatically upon vendor creation, or whether a spend tier must be explicitly assigned. Is there a process that sets spend tier, or does the system assign bronze as a default if no explicit assignment occurs?

source_references.excerpt: Every vendor gets a spend tier. Bronze by default if nobody's assessed them.

ambiguities.description: Purchase order control timing: The transcript states 'The control at creation' prevents raising a PO against a non-active vendor, but it is unclear whether this means (a) the system enforces it at the moment of PO creation (e.g., a form validation or API check), or (b) a downstream step rejects the PO if the vendor is not active. The discussion of Mei's Tuesdays (angry buyers whose POs fail) suggests the control is at creation time, but this should be explicit.

source_references.excerpt: That's the control at creation.

ambiguities.description: Post-suspension purchase order behavior: The transcript explicitly leaves unresolved what happens to in-flight purchase orders when a vendor is suspended. Raj argues suspension should halt everything; Dana argues suspension should allow existing orders to complete (run-off mode). This is noted as parked for the steering group. The model should not assume a constraint here, but stakeholders should clarify: Is suspension hard (all orders halt), soft (existing orders run), or undefined pending policy decision?

source_references.excerpt: My position is that everything halts immediately... we need a middle state. Something like run-off... Parking it explicitly: what happens to in-flight purchase orders when a vendor is suspended is undecided.

ambiguities.description: Region split planning: The transcript notes 'There's been talk of splitting EMEA but it hasn't happened,' implying the set of four region codes (EMEA, APAC, NA, LATAM) may change in the future. Should the region code value constraint be marked mutable, or is the current fixed set sufficient for this model?

source_references.excerpt: Four regions, fixed?... There's been talk of splitting EMEA but it hasn't happened.

ambiguities.description: Overloaded term 'tier': The transcript reveals 'tier' is used with two distinct meanings: spend tier (bronze, silver, gold) owned by procurement, and risk tier (low, medium, high) owned by compliance. While the model separates them as distinct attributes, the ambiguity persists in conversation ('that's a high tier vendor' causes confusion). This is a terminology/communication issue rather than a data model issue, but stakeholders flagged it as 'genuine chaos.' No constraint changes are needed, but awareness is critical for implementation.

source_references.excerpt: We both call it tier and it causes genuine chaos... Two separate fields, different values, different owners.

ambiguities.description: Temporal current-review semantics: The transcript clarifies a vendor accumulates reviews over time and 'one of them is the current signed-off one.' The model does not capture temporal state (e.g., review effective date, expiration, or re-review cycle mentioned at line 105). A vendor may have multiple reviews, but exactly one is 'current'—is this current-ness determined by date ordering, an explicit 'current' flag, or some other mechanism? Without temporal modeling, it is unclear how to determine which review is current when multiple signed-off reviews exist.

source_references.excerpt: we re-review on a cycle, and every re-review is a new record, we don't edit the old one. But one of them is the current signed-off one.

ambiguities.description: Vendor vendor-region-contact relationship cardinality: The model shows 'Vendor operates in Region with Contact' is mandatory on Contact, meaning every contact participates in exactly one (vendor, region) pair. However, it is unclear whether a single contact person could serve multiple (vendor, region) combinations, or whether a contact is exclusively tied to one vendor-region pair. Can the same contact (same contact ID) be reused across different vendors or regions?

source_references.excerpt: It's the combination of the vendor and the region that determines the contact... You cannot have two people both flagged primary for the same vendor in the same region.
